messages:
Mia: quick sync — customer X asked for a committed onboarding path: performance baseline, pin window, and a migration SLA. need to negotiate scope before we promise anything.
Ryan: noted. what does customer mean by 'performance baseline'? p99 latency or throughput?
Mia: they care about tail latency at realistic payloads (avg seq len ~ 256) and cost buckets. asks: p95 < 120ms, per-request cost delta < 1.2x over our hosted default.
Alex: p95 120ms for 256 tokens is tight on some mid-tier models. we can hit it with dedicated GPUs + KV cache; hosted may need warmups.
Sarah: customer is enterprise, willing to pay more for dedicated pools and a 6-month pinned model window. they want rollback guarantees if quality regresses.
Mia: so proposed product commitments: (1) onboarding benchmark: perf + quality on their eval set, (2) pin window: 6 months with optional paid extensions, (3) migration SLA: 30-day notice + assisted migration plan + opt-out for major regressions. thoughts?
Ryan: technical constraints: pinned models on Dedicated are straightforward. For Hosted, pinning implies reservation of capacity or fallbacks to compatible variant. we need a routing policy defined: primary pinned variant -> fallback family.
Alex: agree. must also define acceptable quality delta thresholds to trigger escape hatch. propose: BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity delta < 2% absolute or model-specific metric agreed in onboarding.
Sarah: customer flagged data residency + audit logs as must-haves. will not accept black-box rollouts. need observability hooks for token-level traces for first 2 weeks of cutover.
Mia: add to commitments: observability retention for onboards (30d retention for token traces) and a customer-facing dashboard for rollout progress.
Ryan: ops ask: autoscale / burst policy for their pinned lane. they want predictable throughput during launches. That means reserved headroom + burst credit. estimate +30% capacity buffer during initial 2-week ramp.
Alex: on benchmarking: we should run a three-stage eval: smoke perf (latency/throughput), quality sweep (their eval set + our adversarial prompts), and soak test (72h production-like traffic). Passing criteria must be explicit.
Mia: draft pass criteria: smoke perf: p95 <= 120ms on their payloads; quality: metric deltas within agreed thresholds; soak: error rate < 0.5% and token-error variance within X. if any fail -> remediation / rollback.
Sarah: legal will want wording on rollback triggers vs advisory warnings. i'll loop legal. also customer asks for a one-time migration credit if we ask them to move within pin window.
Mia: migration credit: propose a sliding scale credit based on time left in pin window: >4 months = 30% credit, 1-4 months = 15%, <1 month = 5%.
Ryan: implementation notes: need a canary policy that routes 10% -> new candidate model for 48h, with automatic rollback if monitoring shows quality or latency regressions. include manual override for customer.
Alex: also need to define pin-exception escapes: security patches, critical stability fixes — we should allow emergency swaps but notify customer and offer remediation credits.
Mia: scope negotiation for MVP: (A) onboarding bench + pass criteria doc, (B) pin window + billing attachment, (C) migration SLA + credit table, (D) ops playbook for ramp/cutover including canary config. everything else (observability dashboard UX polish, long-term retention options) is post-MVP.
Sarah: customer asked for SLAs on latency — are we comfortable committing a p95 SLA for pinned models? that has infra implications.
Ryan: we can offer a paid SLA tier on Dedicated only. Hosted pinned lane can have best-effort with SLOs but not SLA until we have capacity guarantees.
Mia: decision: commit to SLA only on Dedicated. Offer hosted pinned contracts with explicit SLOs + escalation path.
Sarah: customer ok with Dedicated-only SLA as long as pricing reflects it.
Mia: action items: @Ryan create ops playbook + canary config template (due EOD Fri). @Alex write benchmark harness + pass/fail thresholds (due Tue). @Sarah gather legal/customer contract asks and confirm migration credit acceptance (due Mon). i'll draft the product commitment doc after those are in.
DevOpsBot: reminder — created checklist: /tasks create "onboard-customer-X-playbook" assigned to @Ryan,@Alex,@Sarah, due 1765490000.
Alex: one more: define escape hatch metrics and the exact artifact we store for 'quality snapshot' (we should store eval set inputs + model outputs + embeddings).
Ryan: storage cost note: retention of token traces + outputs for 30d will change cost profile. will include estimate in playbook.
Mia: good catch. let's reconvene after deliverables. final ask: try to keep pass criteria conservative so we avoid rework during legal/customer reviews. :thumbsup:
Sarah: :thumbsup: thanks all, i'll start the contract thread with the customer and share back any redlines.
